digest: HEAD 654f639 changes three public-facing behaviors in the stop/cancel/terminal path: the summary field launchRetryAttempts is renamed to launchRetries (SPEC T3 calls the old name public), the stop poll default moves from 50ms to 200ms, and cancellation detection widens to 'cancelled'/'timeout'. The code now contradicts SPEC.md, and no tests exist to catch it. Not safe to ship until the rename is resolved and tests cover these paths.

impacts.change: launchRetryAttempts renamed to launchRetries with no alias or deprecation path. SPEC T3 names launchRetryAttempts as a public contract read by external tools.
impacts.risk: Any external consumer reading launchRetryAttempts gets undefined or a parse failure. This is a silent breaking change to a shared data shape.
impacts.evidence: grep: no in-repo reader of launchRetryAttempts; SPEC.md:35 names it as public

impacts.change: Default pollMs changed from 50ms (SPEC S3) to 200ms in code.
impacts.risk: Stop intent is noticed up to 200ms later, which can slow stop-to-abort latency and widens the window where a stop request races with stage completion. Callers that pass pollMs explicitly are unaffected. SPEC S3 also sets a 10ms floor that the code does not appear to enforce; it uses Math.max(1, ...).

impacts.change: Accepted markers widened from SPEC C1 exact set (aborted/AbortError/ABORT_ERR) to include 'cancelled' and 'timeout'.
impacts.risk: Provider returns or errors containing 'timeout' are now classified as cancellation. That can change retry, terminal status, and summary counts for non-cancel failures (false positives). Whether the widening is a fix depends on real provider shapes, which are unverified.
impacts.evidence: implementation-map control: changedByHead likely; u5 unresolved

impacts.change: No unit test files exist (Glob over **/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js,mjs} returned nothing). The only verification script is typecheck. SPEC Q1 requires a test per S/C/T item.
impacts.risk: None of the three behavior changes is verified. Typecheck cannot catch a runtime field rename or a marker-set change.
impacts.evidence: change-scope control assumptions; package.json scripts.typecheck only

impacts.component: SPEC.md S3, C1, T3 vs src/
impacts.change: Code diverges from the spec in four places. The spec was not updated by HEAD and is the stated contract.
impacts.risk: Consumers and reviewers using SPEC.md will assume the old behavior.
impacts.evidence: implementation-map control: SPEC contradicts code in 4 places

impacts.change: Not changed as far as the evidence shows. store.js and types.js are absent from the repo, so the on-disk stop-intent format and record shapes could not be checked.
impacts.risk: Unknown whether persisted run records or control.json consumers depend on the renamed field.

assumptions.text: The changed-file list (workflow-stop.ts, workflow-cancellation.ts, workflow-terminal.ts) is inferred from the commit message and grep, not from git diff. The git diff could not be read in this run, so the exact line-level delta is unverified.
SPEC.md was not modified by 654f639. Mismatches are treated as code-vs-spec drift, not as a spec update.
WorkflowTerminalSummary is computed on read (summarizeWorkflowTerminal) and not persisted. This was not verified because store.js is absent.
Stop-latency and false-positive effects are inferred from the code. No runtime measurement was taken.
